Assertion (A): Section 10 of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970 empowers the appropriate Government to prohibit the employment of contract labour in any process, operation, or other work in any establishment.
Reason (R): This power is exercised unilaterally by the Government without any requirement to consult any advisory body.
options_english: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

key_facts: Section 10 empowers the government to prohibit contract labour employment.

questions.question_english: A contractor supplying security guards to several Directorate of Education schools in Delhi has his licence suspended by the licensing officer without being given an opportunity to show cause. Is this legally sound?
options_english: Yes, because the licensing officer possesses absolute statutory discretionary power to suspend any licence immediately.
Yes, provided that the registered principal employer formally requested the immediate suspension of the licence.
No, because only the jurisdictional High Court holds the legal authority to suspend a contractor’s valid licence.
No, Section 14 mandates giving the licence holder a reasonable opportunity to show cause.
questions.explanation_english: Section 14(1) mandates that before revoking or suspending a licence, the licensing officer must give the contractor a reasonable opportunity of showing cause. Action taken without affording this statutory opportunity violates natural justice and contravenes express provisions of the Act.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (d) है। धारा 14(1) के अनुसार, किसी लाइसेंस को रद्द करने या निलंबित करने से पहले, लाइसेंसिंग अधिकारी को ठेकेदार को कारण बताने का एक उचित अवसर देना चाहिए। इस वैधानिक अवसर के बिना कार्रवाई करना प्राकृतिक न्याय का उल्लंघन करता है और अधिनियम के स्पष्ट प्रावधानों का उल्लंघन करता है।
questions.topic: Contract Labour Abolition and Regulation Act 1970
key_facts: Section 14 mandates giving the licence holder a reasonable opportunity to show cause.
Printed answer key: (D) No, Section 14 mandates giving the licence holder a reasonable opportunity to show cause.

questions.question_english: According to Section 2(1)(b) of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, a workman is deemed to be employed as 'contract labour' in an establishment when he is hired in connection with the work of an establishment by or through:
options_english: Direct recruitment undertaken by the HR department of the Principal Employer
An official government employment exchange or national career portal service
A contractor, with or without the knowledge of the principal employer
A competitive examination conducted by the State Public Service Commission
questions.explanation_english: Section 2(1)(b) defines contract labour as a workman hired in or in connection with the work of an establishment by or through a contractor. The definition explicitly includes situations where hiring occurs with or without the knowledge of the principal employer, establishing a legal employment relationship focused on contractual work execution.
questions.explanation_hindi: सही उत्तर (c) है। धारा 2(1)(b) अनुबंध श्रम को एक श्रमिक के रूप में परिभाषित करती है जिसे एक प्रतिष्ठान के काम से संबंधित काम के लिए एक ठेकेदार के द्वारा या उसके माध्यम से नियुक्त किया जाता है। परिभाषा स्पष्ट रूप से उन स्थितियों को शामिल करती है जहां भर्ती प्रधान नियोक्ता के ज्ञान के साथ या बिना होती है, जो अनुबंध कार्य निष्पादन पर केंद्रित एक कानूनी रोजगार संबंध स्थापित करती है।
questions.topic: Contract Labour Abolition and Regulation Act 1970
key_facts: Section 2(1)(b) defines contract labour.
Includes hiring with or without the principal employer's knowledge.
Establishes a legal employment relationship.
Printed answer key: (c) A contractor, with or without the knowledge of the principal employer.
